fieldValues.title: Default editing mode in the essay editor
fieldValues.decision_question: Which editing mode does a writer get by default, and where does the choice to switch live?
fieldValues.context: The owner, 2026-11-06 (vignette 50a11c7c): a visual editor that does not require markdown knowledge, '(I would like to switch it off and use markdown if I want)'. The editor already keeps per-viewer conveniences in localStorage (src/lib/columns.ts, actor name). Precedent consulted: that pattern; persona 5a603ae9 First-time writer; remedy ecc44c03. Placement: the editor group's log, srs-web.
fieldValues.friction: A default of markdown leaves the barrier for exactly the person this is for; a visual mode with no way out takes the source away from those who want it.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered:
A. Visual by default, with an 'Edit as markdown' switch remembered per browser (recommended). For: serves the new writer with no action on their part; matches existing per-viewer storage; no new server state. Against: the owner must switch once per browser; the choice does not follow a writer across devices.
B. Markdown by default, visual opt-in. For: nothing changes for current writers. Against: the writer who needs it most will not find it.
C. Per-account preference. For: follows the writer. Against: the editor is local-first and has no account requirement, so this needs new state and sign-in.
D. Per-paragraph toggle. For: fine control. Against: more controls on every paragraph, and the render guard already handles the paragraphs that need source.
E. Ask on first run. For: explicit. Against: asks a new writer about a word they may not know, which is the problem being solved.
fieldValues.key_requirements: A first-time writer never has to know the word markdown; a fluent writer can always reach the source; no new server state. 'Markdown help' appears in markdown mode, where it is useful.
fieldValues.decision_statement: The essay editor opens paragraphs visually unless the writer has chosen markdown on that browser.
fieldValues.rationale: Defaults serve the person who cannot be expected to change them, and a fluent writer loses one click. Per-browser storage is what the editor already does for this kind of preference.
fieldValues.revisit_when: Writers regularly lose the setting between devices, or most returning writers switch to markdown, which would call the default or the visual editor into question.
